scaling.linear_threshold: pre-declared in the producer: linear iff speedup >= 0.80 * N = 3.2 at N=4; measured 2.997 (pooled) — sub-linear, justified below
scaling.sub_linear_scale_justification: Measured mechanisms, not excuses: (1) CHAIN-BOUND TAIL — with 4 chains x 2 sequential missions the ideal wall is 2 missions = 12s; the measured 4w median 17.044s carries ~5s of irreducible per-chain scheduling overhead (dispatch + settlement + product_e2e per milestone) that parallelism cannot remove, while the 1w arm pays it 8 times (51.076s); (2) DAEMON POLL SERIALIZATION — the supervisor loop harvests and dispatches advances sequentially every 50ms, so engine starts and settlements queue behind each other (17 engine-overlap pairs per 4w run vs 50 total shows real but partial overlap: engines overlap only after their dispatch serialized); (3) SETTLEMENT SERIALIZATION — PROJECT_STATE writes and attempt-ledger fsyncs serialize per project; (4) the same mechanisms already measured at SCALE_2 (per-worker efficiency 0.861 at 2w on a 2-chain workload) persist at 4 chains (0.749): efficiency DROPS as N rises because the serialized overhead is a growing fraction of the shorter walls. Linear scaling (>= 3.2x) was NOT measured and is NOT claimed.

reliability.decision_rule_predeclared: receipt-level rule (mirrors SCALE_2's conjunction): SCALE_N only if throughput improved AND reliability non-regressed vs the SCALE_2 baseline state AND isolation perfect at N; the producer's arm-level rule (committed BEFORE any 6s evidence ran, factory_v2/run_scale_n_benchmark.py 3f9e21c81) additionally required reliability at Nw no worse than at the same-session 2w arm
reliability.defect_detail: run_0 (2 workers): P4_REUSE launched TWICE (launches_per_mission P4_REUSE=2), 17x p4:STALE_GENERATION_WRITE_BLOCKED cycles, final mission state PASS with lease_generation=2 (P4_BUILD stayed 1), wall 34.448s (+17.7% vs the clean-2w median 29.261s of runs 1-2), still settled 8/8. Fencing held (no double settlement, no concurrent same-mission engines — same_mission_concurrent_overlaps empty).
reliability.defect_mechanism: the SAME unfixed SCALE_2 defect F1: in the window between the engine process EXITING and its settlement being written, the worker heartbeat is gone, so a sibling advance on the same project legitimately sees 'no live worker + not settled' and re-dispatches the mission (new lease generation); the first advance's settlement is then refused as stale generation until the second attempt settles. Impossible at MAX_WORKERS=1 (no sibling dispatcher exists).
reliability.regression_verdict: REGRESSION_NOT_EXCLUDED: reliability non-regression vs SCALE_2 is UNMET. The pooled 4w sample is 8/8 clean, but (a) the known-unfixed F1 defect fired AGAIN in THIS session at the 2-worker arm (defect_detail above — it is live at multi-worker scheduling on this workload), and (b) a clean sample of 8 cannot affirm non-regression against a probabilistic defect: Clopper-Pearson 95% lower bound for 8/8 is 0.631, below the canonical 2w clean rate 10/11 = 0.909, and P(8/8 clean | true rate = canonical 1/11) = (10/11)^8 = 0.467 — an unremarkable outcome under the defect hypothesis. Recommending N workers while the same benchmark session catches the unfixed race at 2 workers would over-claim; the honest verdict is NO_SCALE until F1 is fixed and re-benchmarked (exactly the followup SCALE_2 already named).
reliability.producer_arm_rule_output: SCALE_N_RECOMMENDED (main sample: throughput strictly increasing 0.15663 < 0.26345 < 0.45424, isolation 3/3 perfect at 4w, 4w clean 3/3 >= 2w clean 2/3, real parallelism 50 overlaps) — recorded here for transparency: the producer's pre-declared arm rule passed on its own sample, and the receipt-level decision STILL returns NO_SCALE because the arm rule does not weigh the live F1 defect against the SCALE_2 baseline (clause 'aucune regression vs SCALE_2'), which the receipt-level rule above does. The gate (verify_scale_n_benchmark.py) recomputes the arm rule from its own fresh observation and refuses only an unsupported SCALE_N_RECOMMENDED; this receipt's conservative NO_SCALE can never be refused by it.

decision.rule: scale only if throughput improved AND reliability non-regressed vs the SCALE_2 baseline AND isolation perfect at N workers
decision.consequence: FACTORY_MAX_WORKERS stays 1 (no default flip, no operational change). The measured 4-worker throughput (+199.7% pooled, efficiency 0.749/worker, sub-linear with documented mechanisms) and perfect isolation at N=4 are real, but the conjunction fails on reliability-vs-SCALE_2: the unfixed re-dispatch defect F1 fired again this session at 2 workers and cannot be excluded at 4 by a clean 8-run sample.
decision.followup_named: unchanged from SCALE_2: close the engine-exited->settlement-written liveness gap for sibling advances (settlement-intent marker consulted by the in-flight guard), then re-run this exact N benchmark (both producers are committed and hermetic for that purpose)

unmet_and_notes: Acceptance clause 'aucune regression vs SCALE_2' is UNMET with evidence and reasoning in reliability.regression_verdict — left unmet rather than asserted, per the mission stop conditions.

Acceptance clauses MET with measured evidence: 'N > 2 workers testes avec workload reel' (4 workers, 8 arm runs + drill on the real daemon), 'throughput scale lineairement ou justification documentee' (sub-linear measured + sub_linear_scale_justification with measured mechanisms), 'isolation contextuelle parfaite a N workers' (8/8 4w runs, 15/15 all runs), 'D019 fan-out elastique et reutilisation de connaissance inter-produits sans partage d'autorite' (DEMONSTRATED_AT_4W).

The workload width differs from SCALE_2_W1 by necessity (4 chains instead of 2 — a 2-chain workload cannot distinguish 4 workers from 2); per-mission cost is matched (6.385 vs 6.369 s/mission at 1w) so per-worker efficiency is comparable; absolute throughputs are NOT compared across workloads and no such comparison is claimed.

The gate factory_v2/verify_scale_n_benchmark.py was the fail-closed exit-2 stub until this mission; it now re-runs the committed producer and recomputes the arm rule from raw per-run files (SCALE_2 precedent ef89a19aa, coherence DEFERRED entry removed per precedent a1823326f). Its fresh 2-repeat observation is a NEW sample each run: it can only refuse an unsupported SCALE_N_RECOMMENDED claim; this receipt's NO_SCALE is conservative and always acceptable.
